beats.say: Your Spark cluster runs all night, and sits idle all day.
You pay for machines that do nothing. And every team wants its own version.
beats.label: The pain
beats.head: Idle machines, version fights

beats.say: This port has three steps: operators, Spark and Airflow, and a lane for batch.
beats.label: Port 12 · Data platforms

check.prompt: You create a custom resource and nothing happens. What do you check first?
check.why: A custom resource is only data. The operator is the controller that acts on it.

beats.say: First: teach the cluster a new object.
A custom resource definition adds a new kind. For example: a Spark application.
beats.label: A new kind
beats.head: A new kind in the API

beats.say: An operator is a controller for that kind. It does the manual steps for you.
beats.label: Operator
beats.head: A control loop you install

check.prompt: In Spark on Kubernetes, who asks for the executor pods?
check.why: The driver asks the API server for executors, so its service account needs that permission.

beats.say: Second: one pod per piece of work.
beats.text: A pod per piece of work

beats.say: Each Spark job gets its own driver pod. The driver asks for executor pods.
beats.label: Spark
beats.head: The driver asks for executors

beats.say: When the job ends, the pods go away. You pay for the run only.
beats.label: No idle cluster
beats.head: Pods leave when the job ends

beats.say: Airflow can do the same: every task runs in its own pod.
beats.label: Airflow
beats.head: One pod per task

beats.say: Third: keep batch away from serving.
Use a tainted node pool, a low priority, and a quota for each team.
beats.label: Three guards

beats.say: A taint only keeps other pods out. Add a node selector to keep batch in.
beats.label: The trap
beats.head: Taint plus a node selector

beats.say: Operators add new kinds. Jobs bring their own pods. And batch gets its own lane.
beats.label: Data platforms

beats.say: Now start the first lesson below.
